headline: Medium risk: shared data/workflow surfaces create leakage and cascade paths; prompt injection is limited by no browser and no shared channel evidence.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow has broad network egress but no browser, while Plane exposes file uploads and issue/task content. No shared channel or direct ingestion path is documented, so prompt injection is not provable; however, if operators manually move Airflow outputs into Plane notes/files, malicious content could be reinterpreted as instructions.
conditions: IF operators copy Airflow-generated text into Plane notes, issues, or file uploads
IF Plane workflows treat uploaded text as instructions without sanitization
mitigations: Restrict manual copy-paste between systems
Add a review step before importing Airflow output into Plane
Use plain-text templates with instruction markers stripped
Train operators to treat imported content as untrusted

B_data_leakage.rationale: Airflow can egress broadly, and Plane handles files, notes, hyperlinks, and issue/task content. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem or explicit sensitive-data class, but a default workflow that moves files or task content from Airflow into Plane can expose work products to another service path. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Airflow tasks export files or task payloads into Plane uploads or notes
IF those payloads contain sensitive work products
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in shared workflows
Redact payloads before transfer
Limit Plane uploads to non-sensitive artifacts
Audit Airflow DAGs that emit documents or logs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow is a data orchestrator with broad egress, while Plane supports multiple instances and file uploads but shows write_filesystem=false. The profiles do not indicate both agents can write the same directory or mutate shared git state, so direct write conflict is not established. Any conflict would require an external shared mutable resource not documented here.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same external mutable resource
IF an orchestrator grants Plane filesystem write through a wrapper not shown in the profile
mitigations: Separate storage targets per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared resources
Use locking on any shared database or queue
Review deployment for hidden write paths

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow can generate automated outputs, and Plane stores issues/tasks/roadmaps that may be used operationally. If Airflow-produced facts are imported into Plane without verification, Plane can propagate incorrect scheduling or issue decisions. The profiles do not show explicit action-taking like email sending, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF Plane treats Airflow output as authoritative input
IF no human verification step exists before creating or updating issues
mitigations: Require human review before Plane updates
Add source links to every imported item
Flag imported Airflow outputs as unverified
Use validation checks on critical fields

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only and do not declare regulated data classes, residency, or retention mismatches. Airflow touches no data classes in the profile, while Plane touches files and notes, so compliance risk is limited to generic policy mismatch rather than a documented breach. The other agent is not cited beyond confirming the pair context.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane files or notes
IF Airflow exports that regulated data into a deployment with stricter residency or retention rules
mitigations: Classify data before transfer
Block regulated data in Plane uploads
Document retention settings for both systems
Review residency requirements for any shared deployment
